name: 1973 oil embargo
event: Arab oil producers cut exports to countries supporting Israel.
effects: Oil price roughly quadrupled within a few months (about $3 to about $12 a barrel); fuel shortages and queues in the US; inflation and recession followed in many rich countries.

name: 1990 Iraq invades Kuwait
event: Iraq invades Kuwait; oil supply from both countries is cut off.
effects: Oil price more than doubled in about two months (from under $20 to about $40 a barrel at the peak in October 1990), then fell back after the war started in January 1991.

name: 1997 Asian financial crisis
event: Currency crisis spreads from Thailand to Indonesia and South Korea.
effects: The Korean won lost about half its value against the dollar within weeks; Korea took an IMF rescue loan; unemployment rose sharply in 1998.

name: 2008 Lehman Brothers collapse
event: A large US investment bank goes bankrupt in a housing and credit crisis.
effects: US stocks (S&P 500) fell about 57% from the 2007 peak to the March 2009 low; central banks cut rates to near zero; global recession.

name: 2010-2011 food price spike
event: Drought and export bans push global grain prices up.
effects: The FAO food price index reached a record in early 2011; high bread prices were one of the pressures behind the Arab Spring protests.

name: 2016 Brexit vote
event: The UK votes to leave the European Union.
effects: The British pound fell about 8% against the dollar the next day, to a 31-year low.

name: 2020 COVID-19 shock
event: A pandemic and lockdowns stop much of the world economy.
effects: US stocks fell about 34% in about one month (February to March 2020); unemployment jumped; central banks cut rates to near zero; oil prices collapsed.

name: 2021 Suez Canal blockage
event: The container ship Ever Given blocks the Suez Canal for six days.
effects: Hundreds of ships queued; about 12% of world trade passes the canal; shipping delays lasted weeks after it reopened.

name: 2022 Russia invades Ukraine
effects: Oil rose from under $100 to about $128 a barrel within two weeks; wheat prices rose sharply because Russia and Ukraine are big exporters; European gas prices hit records later in 2022; inflation rose in Europe.

name: 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure
event: After US and Israeli strikes on Iran, Iran announces it is closing the Strait of Hormuz (about 15 million barrels of crude a day normally pass).
effects: Crude rose about 10% to near $80 a barrel on the first day; the closure lasted much longer than first expected; Fitch expected Brent at $100 to $110 from May to July 2026.
